section_summary: This section documents United States and Allied interdepartmental actions between January and August 1947 concerning the custody, microfilming, and disposition of Japanese diplomatic and consular archives and official property abroad, including operations in Italy, Argentina, and Portugal. It details inter-agency planning for the Japanese War Documents Project to publish Japanese foreign policy records dating from the 1890s through World War II. It also records Allied diplomatic consultations with the Soviet Union, China, and Great Britain regarding access to central Japanese government archives in Tokyo and the custody of consular court records in China.

subfiles.about: Transmitting diplomatic correspondence with the Soviet Foreign Ministry concerning Japanese diplomatic archives abroad and Soviet access to central archives in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Moscow transmits correspondence with Soviet Deputy Foreign Minister Vyshinski regarding proposals for disposing of Japanese diplomatic property abroad and Soviet requests for equal access to central Japanese government archives in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 704: Disposition of the Archives and Property of the Former Japanese Consular and Diplomatic Establishments Abroad

subfiles.about: Inquiring about microfilming procedures, warehouse storage, and resolving competing Allied claims for Japanese records in Rome.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Rome reports readiness to microfilm Japanese diplomatic documents, asking about duplicate copies, warehouse storage, and resolving competing Allied claims.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-30: Microfilming and Storage of Japanese Diplomatic and Consular Documents

subfiles.about: Instructing Embassy Rome on specific documents to microfilm, storage authorization, and handling Allied requests.
subfiles.summary: The State Department directs Embassy Rome to microfilm specified records, authorizes warehouse storage of original archives, and advises using reproductions.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 145 to Rome: Microfilming and Handling of Japanese Records

subfiles.about: Submitting quarterly accounting statements and vouchers for the Allied trusteeship of Japanese funds in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Despatch transmits the quarterly account current for the quadripartite trusteeship of Japanese official and private funds in Buenos Aires. It includes bank transfer documentation, cash account reconciliations, and receipts for cable expenses incurred in repatriating twenty-two Japanese civilians to Japan via Shanghai.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1664: Accounts of Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds, October 14–December 31, 1946

subfiles.about: Duplicate ozalid copy of despatch transmitting trusteeship accounts.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate ozalid copy of despatch transmitting quarterly accounts of the Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds in Buenos Aires.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1664: Accounts of Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds, October 14–December 31, 1946 (Duplicate Ozalid Copy)

subfiles.about: Reporting Soviet agreement in principle to diplomatic property plan and Soviet request for access to Tokyo central archives.
subfiles.summary: Informs SCAP that the Soviet Government accepted in principle the diplomatic property plan but requested access to Tokyo central archives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 4332 to Tokyo: Soviet Reaction to Plan for Japanese Diplomatic Property and Archives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Designating a replacement white record copy of Telegram 199 for central files.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Communications and Records)
subfiles.summary: Designates an attached white copy of Telegram 199 as the permanent record copy to replace the missing action copy.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Record Copy Designation for Telegram 199

subfiles.about: Correcting a translation error regarding points B and C in the Soviet reply on Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Embassy Moscow clarifies that proposed Soviet text changes applied to point B rather than point C due to Cyrillic transliteration.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 199 from Moscow: Translation Correction Regarding Proposed Note

subfiles.about: Inquiring about Japanese Foreign Office archives held by SCAP International Prosecution Section and ATIS.
subfiles.summary: Instructs SCAP Political Adviser to check Japanese Foreign Office document availability with IPS and ATIS back to 1890.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 30 to Tokyo: Availability of Japanese Foreign Office Archives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Proposing a scholarly publication series of Japanese diplomatic papers relating to World War II.
subfiles.summary: Proposes a United States project to publish Japanese diplomatic papers from the 1890s through World War II.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Proposed Publication of Japanese War Documents
subfiles.to: William Benton, H. Freeman Matthews, John Carter Vincent, Dean Acheson

subfiles.about: Japanese Government request for return of former consular court and administrative records held in China.
subfiles.summary: Reports Japanese requests for return of consular court and administrative records in China, requesting Embassy Nanking seek Chinese concurrence.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 32 from Tokyo: Return of Japanese Consular Archives in China

subfiles.about: Requesting an urgent reply to State Department telegram of January 29 regarding Japanese archives.
subfiles.summary: Requests an expedited reply to State Department telegram of January 29 regarding Japanese Foreign Office archives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 56 to Tokyo: Request for Reply on Foreign Office Archives
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmitting War Department confirmation that the United States holds exclusive title to captured Japanese documents in Washington.
subfiles.from: W. C. Affeld, Jr. (Central Intelligence Group)
subfiles.summary: Transmits a War Department intelligence memorandum confirming exclusive United States title to captured Japanese documents in the Washington Document Center.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Ownership of and Agreements Concerning Captured Japanese Documents

subfiles.about: Legal opinion affirming United States title to captured Japanese documents and authority to publish them unilaterally.
subfiles.summary: Advises that the United States Government holds title to captured Japanese documents in Washington and may publish them unilaterally.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Title to the Japanese Documents in Washington Document Center

subfiles.about: Explaining United States policy regarding Chinese retention and permitted inspection of Japanese consular archives in China.
subfiles.summary: Explains China's willingness to allow inspection of Japanese consular archives while refusing release, concurring China retains custody under SCAP directives.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 150 to Tokyo / No. 252 to Nanking: Retention and Inspection of Japanese Archives in China
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo / American Embassy, Nanking

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether disputed Japanese documents divided among Allied embassies may remain with them provided accessibility is assured.
subfiles.summary: Reports division of disputed Japanese Embassy records among Allied embassies in Rome, asking if US access guarantees are sufficient.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 406 from Rome: Microfilming and Distribution of Disputed Japanese Records

subfiles.about: Approving division of Japanese archives among Allied embassies while emphasizing preservation and accessibility.
subfiles.summary: Agrees to administrative dispersion of Japanese archives among Allied embassies in Rome, preferring originals kept together and requiring guaranteed accessibility.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-135 to Rome: Dispersion and Preservation of Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Interdepartmental coordination and draft cable proposing publication of Japanese foreign policy documents from the 1890s through World War II.
subfiles.from: P. Sullivan, G. Bernard Noble, Ernest A. Gross
subfiles.summary: Internal State Department memoranda, War Department liaison correspondence, and draft cables coordinate a formal proposal to SCAP for publishing Japanese diplomatic papers from the 1890s through World War II. The proposal outlines sending five scholars to Japan and requests SCAP assistance with microfilming, clerical staff, and living quarters. Costs of Japanese-language publication are proposed to be charged to the Japanese economy as an occupation expense.
subfiles.title: Memoranda and Draft Cable on the Proposed Japanese War Documents Project
subfiles.to: Charles R. Cameron, Col. Chard, Col. Gross, SCAP

subfiles.about: Inquiring whether unseized Japanese war documents remain intact or should be impounded by SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether unseized Japanese war documents are complete or tampered with, and whether SCAP should be advised to impound them.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 72 to Tokyo: Appraisal and Impounding of Japanese War Documents
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Unsent draft cable outlining proposed Japanese diplomatic papers publication project to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Unsent draft telegram detailing State Department plans to publish Japanese diplomatic documents dating from the 1890s and requesting SCAP assistance.
subfiles.title: Draft Telegram to Tokyo on Japanese War Documents Project (Not Sent)
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Reporting evacuation of Japanese ministry archives to Washington Document Center and advising against the War Documents Project in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports evacuation of ministry archives to the Washington Document Center and advises against initiating the war documents appraisal in Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 67 from Tokyo: Status and Evacuation of Japanese Ministry Archives (Pages 2–3)

subfiles.about: Opposing Soviet proposals for quadripartite access to central Japanese government archives in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Strongly opposes granting Allied powers blanket access to central Japanese archives, warning of Soviet interference, surveillance burdens, and incomplete files.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 68 from Tokyo: Objections to Four-Power Access to Central Japanese Archives

subfiles.about: Transmitting eighteen bound volumes of former Japanese Embassy and Consulate records to Washington for microfilming.
subfiles.summary: Forwards eighteen bound Japanese volumes by air pouch for microfilming in Washington, noting local facilities cannot handle bound books.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-612 from Rome: Transmission of Bound Documents for Microfilming

subfiles.about: Notifying that enclosures accompanying Rome Despatch No. 460 were not received with the despatch.
subfiles.from: Department of State (Division of Communications and Records, DC/R)
subfiles.summary: Division of Communications and Records routing slip noting unreceived Japanese document enclosures to Despatch 460 were later returned to Rome.
subfiles.title: Form Slip DC/R: Notice of Unreceived Enclosures to Despatch 460
subfiles.to: Division of Research for Far East (DRO)

subfiles.about: Formally transmitting eighteen bound Japanese Embassy and Consulate volumes to the Department for microfilming.
subfiles.summary: Transmits eighteen bound Japanese diplomatic volumes to Washington by air pouch for microfilming and prompt return to Rome.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 460 from Rome: Transmission of Ex-Japanese Documents for Microfilming

subfiles.about: Returning eighteen bound Japanese documents uncopied because they contained nothing of intelligence value.
subfiles.summary: Informs Embassy Rome that the eighteen Japanese volumes contained nothing of value, were not microfilmed, and are being returned.
subfiles.title: Instruction to Rome: Return of Ex-Japanese Documents Unmicrofilmed

subfiles.about: Recommending Japanese consular property from Los Angeles be transferred to State Department custody in Washington.
subfiles.summary: Recommends FBI deliver former Japanese Consulate Los Angeles archives to State Department custody for storage at the Japanese Embassy in Washington.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to FBI on Personal Property and Archives of Former Japanese Consulate at Los Angeles

subfiles.about: Submitting first quarter 1947 accounts for the Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds in Argentina.
subfiles.summary: Transmits signed quarterly accounts for the quadripartite Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds in Buenos Aires for January through March 1947.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1957 from Buenos Aires: Accounts of Allied Powers Trusteeship Japanese Funds, January 1–March 31, 1947

subfiles.about: Transmitting an offer of an inventor's rifle grenade gauge, a naval code card, and code notes to the War Department.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an inventor's grenade gauge letter, a Japanese naval code card, and code notes to the War Department.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to War Department: Forwarding Materials Found in Former Japanese Embassy
subfiles.to: Chief of Plans and Collection Branch, Pentagon, War Department

subfiles.about: Transmitting citizen service offer letters, a weapon invention letter, a naval code card, and code notes to the FBI.
subfiles.summary: Forwards citizen service offer letters, a grenade gauge proposal, a Japanese naval code card, and code notes to the FBI.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to FBI: Forwarding Materials Found in Former Japanese Embassy

subfiles.about: Transmitting citizen letters, a Japanese naval code card, and Japanese code notes to Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Forwards citizen letters, a Japanese naval code card, and Japanese code notes to the Office of Naval Intelligence.
subfiles.title: Memorandum to ONI: Forwarding Materials Found in Former Japanese Embassy

subfiles.about: Transmitting Lisbon Despatch No. 1481 on official Japanese property and records in Portugal to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Transmits to SCAP for the Civil Property Custodian a copy of the tripartite committee's report on Japanese affairs in Portugal.
subfiles.title: Cover Instruction to SCAP: Report on Japanese Affairs in Portugal
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP), Tokyo

subfiles.about: Transmitting comprehensive joint final report and financial annexes on administering, liquidating, and repatriating Japanese diplomatic affairs in Portugal.
keywords: Bank of London and South America
subfiles.summary: Transmits the final joint report and detailed accounts of the American, British, and Chinese committee charged with administering official Japanese diplomatic property and affairs in Portugal. The committee inventoried chancery and residential property, sold furniture and motor vehicles at public auction, and oversaw the repatriation of Japanese officials and their families to Japan via Barcelona. Remaining balances exceeding thirty-one million escudos were consolidated in a joint bank account in Lisbon awaiting final international disposition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 1481 from Lisbon: Final Report of the Committee's Handling Japanese Affairs in Portugal
